$comment: D-ASM-AARCH64-FP-BARE-OPERAND-WIDTH-DIVERGES-FROM-REFERENCE (R5 + R8, P50) — class-scoped width-view modifier letters, by execution. ★ THE aarch64 ARMS bind BOTH register files in one template: `mov %w0, %w1` / `mov %x0, %x1` run the GPR views inside a real instruction while an FP-class `"w"`-bound double is live in the same statement — the class check is per OPERAND, and the two views must differ in exactly bits 63:32 of the result (a letter decoded at the wrong width moves exactly those bits; a letter refused for the wrong class kills the compile). The FP letters themselves do not appear in an EXECUTED instruction here, and this sentence USED TO give the reason as *the aarch64 gas dialect spells no FP mnemonic* — ✔MEASURED true when written (51 instructions, none floating) and FALSE since P54, which declared seven (`fadd fsub fmul fdiv fneg fcmp fmov`) under D-ASM-DIALECTS-DECLARE-A-REGISTER-CLASS-NO-INSTRUCTION-CAN-NAME. ★ THE EXAMPLE IS UNCHANGED ON PURPOSE: its subject is the class-scoped width-view LETTERS, and `c_inline_asm_arm64_fp_operands` is now the file that executes FP mnemonics — rewriting these templates would trade a pin for a duplicate. Their decode and both refusal directions stay pinned at the asm tier in tests/asm/test_asm_class_scoped_modifiers.cpp. ★ THE x86-64 ARMS run the measured gcc-accepted construct the width-only posture exists to keep: `movsd %q1, %q0` over `"x"`-bound xmm operands (✔gcc renders the bare `%xmm0` — the letter degrades; clang refuses; the disjunction decides acceptance), against the bare control. ⚠ `volatile` seeds are load-bearing: the release arm must still reach the templates. Exit codes name the failing shape.
